questions.question: Why is objective confirmation of asthma important when feasible?
choices: Some patients carrying an asthma label have another condition, and variable airflow limitation should be documented when possible
Asthma can only be diagnosed during an ICU admission
Symptoms never matter
Objective testing should delay emergency treatment
questions.explanation: Asthma is commonly misdiagnosed. Objective evidence helps confirm variable airflow limitation, but acute treatment should not be delayed in a clinically significant exacerbation.

questions.question: What does current asthma control assess?
choices: Recent symptoms, nighttime awakening, activity limitation, and reliever use
Only the patient’s diagnosis date
Only the lung examination during a symptom-free visit
Only age
questions.explanation: Control describes recent burden. Future risk is assessed separately through exacerbation history, medication use, lung function, technique, and other factors.

questions.question: Which is a high-risk asthma feature even if daily symptoms are currently limited?
choices: Recent severe exacerbation or no anti-inflammatory treatment
A working spacer
A completed action plan
No history of nighttime symptoms
questions.explanation: Recent severe exacerbations, poor adherence, incorrect technique, low lung function, high reliever use, and absent anti-inflammatory therapy can increase future risk.

questions.question: Before stepping up chronic asthma therapy, what should the FNP check?
choices: Diagnosis, inhaler technique, adherence, access, triggers, smoking or vaping, and comorbidities
Only the color of the inhaler
Whether the patient wants a stronger medicine without assessment
Nothing if a rescue inhaler is used often
questions.explanation: Apparent treatment failure often results from a wrong diagnosis, incorrect technique, poor adherence, access barriers, exposure, or comorbid disease.

questions.question: Why is inhaled corticosteroid-containing therapy a central asthma principle?
choices: Asthma includes airway inflammation as well as bronchoconstriction, and anti-inflammatory treatment reduces exacerbation risk
Rescue bronchodilator use alone addresses all asthma risk
Corticosteroid-containing inhalers are only for pneumonia
Technique does not matter
questions.explanation: Contemporary asthma care emphasizes anti-inflammatory treatment. The exact strategy follows current guidelines, formulary, patient factors, and clinical severity.

questions.question: Which finding during an asthma flare is most concerning?
choices: Exhaustion, inability to speak in phrases, and markedly diminished breath sounds
A patient comfortably speaking in full sentences
A refill request with no symptoms
A normal inhaler dose counter
questions.explanation: A quiet chest in a distressed patient can signal critically poor airflow. Severe distress, altered mentation, hypoxemia, cyanosis, or poor rescue response requires emergency evaluation.

questions.question: Which is an important differential diagnosis for new wheeze and dyspnea in an older adult?
choices: Heart failure, COPD, infection, pulmonary embolism, or cardiac ischemia depending on context
Asthma only
No condition requires testing
Only seasonal allergy
questions.explanation: New wheeze is not automatically asthma. Red flags and patient context determine the need to consider cardiopulmonary, infectious, vascular, upper-airway, and medication causes.

questions.question: What does a useful written asthma action plan include?
choices: Baseline treatment, early-worsening actions, emergency warning signs, and teach-back
Only the brand name of a rescue inhaler
No need for follow-up
A guarantee that no exacerbation will occur
questions.explanation: Action plans should be plain-language, individualized, feasible, and understood by the patient or caregiver before a flare occurs.

questions.question: When is asthma-specialty referral especially appropriate?
choices: Diagnostic uncertainty, work-related asthma, frequent exacerbations, recurrent systemic steroid need, or persistent symptoms despite verified care
Only after the patient stops all inhalers
Never for adult-onset symptoms
Only for mild transient cough
questions.explanation: Referral helps with uncertain diagnosis, occupational exposure, difficult-to-control disease, severe phenotype assessment, and advanced treatment decisions.

questions.question: A patient has asthma symptoms at work that improve away from work. What is the FNP priority?
choices: Assess possible occupational asthma or work-aggravated disease and arrange objective evaluation/referral
Assume anxiety without questions
Tell the patient to continue the same exposure indefinitely
Use a diagnosis code without assessment
questions.explanation: Work-related symptoms can indicate occupational asthma. Identifying and reducing the relevant exposure and arranging prompt evaluation can protect long-term lung health.
